summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Dress Making ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to modify a T-shirt into a dress using Marvelous Designer. We will create a one-piece lantern sleeve top and make necessary adjustments to ensure a perfect fit. ## Importing the Model First, import the new virtual model, Hanna, from Marvelous Designer and add the default T-shirt to the 3D window. Since the default clothes and Hanna are all wearing the same outfit, you can directly use the automatic adjustment panel tool to modify the T-shirt. ## Adjusting the T-shirt You can see that the size of the T-shirt has been changed to match the body shape of Hanna. To better check the wearing effect of the clothes, change to an A pose. Since Hanna is wearing high heels, you need to click to keep the current shoes posture. As the posture changes, the clothing wearing style also changes. ## Modifying the T-shirt to a Lantern Sleeve Top Next, we will modify the T-shirt to create a one-piece lantern sleeve top. After selecting the line section 3D panel tool, you can draw the line section on the clothes. Click to create the starting point. In the process, press the Ctrl key and then click to draw the line section. ### Drawing the Line Section The line section is the same as drawing the inner line. When the 3D line crosses the part between the panel and the model and has an intersection or the corner is relatively large, it will not be able to be drawn. We can double-click on the panel to end the creation of the 3D line. The purpose of drawing the 3D line here is to make a reference for drawing the inner line, which is easy to locate, so you don't have to draw the back again. ### Drawing the Inner Line Then, use the inner line tool to draw the pattern along the 3D line on the clothing. Note that the starting and end points of the inner line must be aligned with the points on the outer line of the panel. This way, you can accurately cut the line. ## Adjusting the Panel After selecting the inner line, choose the section in the menu bar on the right. You can then select the extra panels and delete them. Since there is no reference to the 3D line in the back panel, we need to change our approach or return to the original 3D line for reference. We need to change the way we draw the inner line. ### Editing the Line Use the tool to edit the line. Select the line that was separated because the panel was deleted. Then select the point at the beginning of the line and add a point. This way, when cutting the back piece, you can ensure that the line remains consistent. ## Final Adjustments Based on this point, draw an inner line, cut the panel, and delete the unnecessary panel. After simulation, check the panel. Turn to the back, and you will see some penetrations. Currently, the surface diameter of Hanna has been reduced to 1. The panel is only attached to the virtual model, but the grid of the panel is too large, causing penetration. Reduce the particle diameter of all panels to 15 to resolve this issue. ### Reducing Conflict Thickness Additionally, reduce the conflict thickness of the panel to make it more suitable for Hanna. When you turn to the back, you can see that the panel size is relatively large. Adjust the width of the back by dragging the back middle line separately. This can keep the curve of the sleeve part unchanged. ## Adjusting the Skeleton Due to the current pose, the arm is close to the body. Press Shift-X to adjust the skeleton. Click on the joint of the arm and then click on the icon on the upper right of the subscribe ball to open the symmetrical edit. Change the posture when opening the simulation. ### Fixing the Chest Panel To prevent the chest panel from moving during the later changes of the action, use the red dot to fix it on the virtual model. In the bottom menu, select the tool to fix the virtual model. Click on the dot on the panel, and then click on the virtual model. After opening the simulation, check the molding effect. ## Adjusting Fabric Types If the position of the panel has formed an obvious deformation, adjust it with the edit molding tool. Copy a fabric type and apply it to the large panel. These large panels are the last ones to be applied to the large panel. We want to give them a fabric that does not easily stretch and deform and is not easy to fold. ### Checking the Effect of Leather Fabric After selecting the leather fabric, open the simulation to check the effect. You can see that the fold of the leather fabric is minimal. Next, adjust the size to fit while selecting the bottom of the front and back panels and dragging the bottom up. In the process, press Shift to move the reference line. ## Using the Transparency Chart Press Alt+4 to open the transparency chart to check the loose material in the clothing. When using the 3D drawing tool, turn on the transparency display and draw a line along the body curve as a reference. Use the plus point line tool to add a straight line on the side of the front panel and the corresponding position on the side of the back panel. ## Finalizing the Design After the simulation, check the wearing effect of the outfit again. Check the side view; you can see that the front is very prominent, and the side curves need modification. Select the point at the bottom of the side to move it inside the board. After the simulation, you can see that due to the changes on the side, the front is more suitable for virtual models. ### Adjusting Points for Better Fit Change the point in the front to flatten the bottom of the board. Click on the highest point of the chest and then click on the point in the corresponding position of the bottom of the board for reference. Use the plus point division tool to add a point to the bottom of the board. Right-click on this point, select Add Render, and enter the corresponding value. ## Connecting Lines and Final Touches Select a group of lines that form a line, adjust their position to connect the top and the highest point of the chest. Pull up the line point along the vertical direction, lengthen the line, and simulate again. After adding a line, the board is more suitable for virtual models. ### Ensuring a Natural Look There may still be some inconsistencies on the side, requiring further adjustments. Separate the two points at the bottom of the line and pull them apart slightly. When combined, the board will appear more natural. Only the leather fabric can achieve such a flat effect due to its high bending intensity. ## Conclusion If you switch back to the default fabric, you will see that there are still some creases. Change back to the leather fabric and simulate again. Since the back needs to be made into a skirt, adjust the top, which is currently a bit long. Select the bottom and move it up, but ensure the bottom remains flat. ### Cutting the Bottom Use a tool to cut out the flat bottom. Expand the 3D window for better visibility. Right-click on the toolbar and click on the clothing measurement tool. After selecting the long button clothing measurement tool, select the circular measurement and clothing. Click on the model near the waist board and use the editor clothing measurement tool to select the green measurement board. ### Final Adjustments to the Panels Right-click and select the bottom of the symmetrical bar. As you can see, the top one is cut along this measurement board. Select the excess boards and delete them. Adjust the straight line point of the bottom board. ## Finalizing the Seam Allowance During cutting, one side of the seam allowance will fall, needing to be added again. After checking, you may find that the side of the seam allowance has been stretched. Use a sewing needle to fix it to the side of the virtual model, repeating the process for the other side. ### Closing Remarks From the back, if the bottom is still tight, repeat the process. With the model open, ensure the arm bone is symmetrical and adjust if necessary. As for the base, you can stop after using all threadchings. ```
